affiliations.occupation: Chauffeur or driver of a bus, taxi, truck, or tractor
affiliations.date_precision: The exact official Army-entry record carries civilian-occupation group 5,7-36 on November 9, 1942. The grouped category names no employer, vehicle type, route, product, or worksite.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms identity. The grouped occupation cannot establish a named employer or the later Army-to-OSS sequence.

affiliations.date_precision: A May 1944 official OSS report says Carosone had been a building custodian in civilian life and entered the Army in July 1943 through OSS after direct recruitment. No employer, building, or exact induction day is named in that report.
affiliations.research_notes: The OSS report and index carry the same private identifier and exact name. Direct OSS recruitment and induction make building custodian the best-supported immediate civilian occupation, but no employer is inferred.

affiliations.date_precision: The exact official Army-entry record carries corrected civilian-status code 992 on April 22, 1943. The official code list defines 9-92 as students but names no school, program, or dates of attendance.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms identity. Student status is not employment; no institution or Army-to-OSS transition date is inferred.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: American Embassy and Consulate General in Istanbul
affiliations.role_title: Local diplomatic-post employee; successive messenger, interpreter, and attaché roles
affiliations.date_precision: The official 1964 profile says Carp's government career began in 1914 as a local employee at the American Embassy, identifies her with the Embassy and Consulate General, and then places her in OSS from 1942 through 1947. It does not date each title or the institutional transition.
affiliations.research_notes: The source directly sequences a continuous government career beginning at the Istanbul diplomatic post and the 1942-1947 OSS assignment. Because it does not use a formula such as 'left X to join OSS,' the transition is strongly date-bounded rather than explicit-immediate. The Department of State is normalized as the employer while the historical post names remain visible.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Betty Carp is very likely Bertha (Betty) Carp, the Istanbul Foreign Service employee assigned to OSS in New York from 1942 to 1947.
claims.evidence_excerpt: From 1942 to 1947 she was assigned to the New York office of the Office of Strategic Services (OSS).
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An official State Department profile supplies the uncommon exact familiar name, the formal name Bertha, a detailed diplomatic-service chronology, and an explicit OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the rare exact name and explicit OSS chronology in an official institutional profile closely match the index, but the accessible source supplies no Box 108 or private-identifier linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: The profile directly dates the OSS assignment to 1942-1947 and the preceding government career to 1914 onward.
claims.match_notes: Bertha and Betty are documented by the source, not inferred. No biographical fact from Wikipedia or another discovery-only page is used as final evidence.
